articles.title: Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield to Receive £20 Million for Community Improvements
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale council is set to accept nearly £20 million in government funding to improve neglected areas, including Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, with plans to enhance local facilities and tackle congestion.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield are set to benefit from nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising these historically overlooked areas. The Rochdale council is expected to accept the Pride in Place funding, amounting to £19.6 million, during a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, 2026. This funding will be distributed over the next decade, providing just under £2 million annually for community improvements.

The local authority has not yet developed a specific plan for how the funds will be allocated. However, early suggestions include tackling congestion, improving parking facilities, creating new green spaces, enhancing local amenities, and expanding maternity services. The council plans to establish a Neighbourhood Board, comprising local community figures, MP Paul Waugh, and council representatives, to oversee the proposal for spending the funds.

Community members have expressed a mix of skepticism and hope regarding the funding. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, noted the area's lack of investment and called for improvements that would benefit children and create community spaces. Another local, Dinah Banks, highlighted the need for better healthcare services and expressed doubt about the effectiveness of the funding. MP Paul Waugh has already conducted consultations with residents to gather their input on potential improvements.

The Neighbourhood Board will have until November 30, 2026, to submit a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, which is necessary to unlock the funding. Initial government support of £150,000 has already been granted to help form the board and develop the plan, marking a significant step towards revitalising these neglected areas of Rochdale.
